doc.title: Hide Tanaka interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 3, 2014

title: Favorite bassists Ray Brown, Sam Jones and Paul Chambers
summary: He names his favorites for their rhythm; Rowe quotes Milt Hinton on providing a rhythmic service.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Who are your three favorite bass players?
Ray Brown, Sam Jones, Paul Chambers. I love their rhythm.

Yes. I can tell. A bass player I think has to have a certain — they have to have their ego in place. I mean that’s my sense of it. You have to be happy providing — as Milt Hinton called it, “providing a rhythmic service” and then you’ll have your moments in the spotlight too.
Yeah. The rhythm is the most important for a jazz bass player.
